issues.title: Client gametest: deadlock in TestSingleplayerContext.close() between deferDisconnect and the phaser
issues.body:
**Versions**
- Minecraft 26.2 with Fabric API 0.160.0+26.2 (fabric-client-gametest-api-v1 6.0.2+0f4f1dca9e). Also seen on Minecraft 26.1.2 with Fabric API 0.155.3+26.1.2 (5.1.0+0a5283664c).
- Fabric Loader 0.19.5, Java 25 (Azul), Arch Linux.
- Other mods in the run: Sodium, Iris, Lithium, Ferrite Core, C2ME, Entity Texture Features, Entity Model Features, Lithostitched, Terralith.

**What happens**

Now and then a client gametest hangs forever while it closes a singleplayer world with `TestSingleplayerContext.close()`. CPU use drops to almost nothing and the window stops answering the desktop. I have seen it three times, in two different tests, each time while several gametest clients ran at the same time on one busy machine. I could not make it happen on purpose.

**Thread state** (two dumps 5 seconds apart, both the same)

Render thread, parked in the server halt that the deferred disconnect started:
```
at net.minecraft.util.thread.BlockableEventLoop.executeBlocking(BlockableEventLoop.java:96)
at net.minecraft.client.server.IntegratedServer.halt(IntegratedServer.java:256)
at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.disconnect(Minecraft.java:2334)
at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.disconnect(Minecraft.java:2298)
at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.lambda$deferDisconnect$0 (fabric-client-gametest-api-v1)
at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.postRunTasks
at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.handler$...$fabric-client-gametest-api-v1$postRunTasksHook
```

Server thread, waiting at the phaser:
```
at java.util.concurrent.Phaser$QNode.block
at net.fabricmc.fabric.impl.client.gametest.threading.ThreadingImpl.enterPhase(ThreadingImpl.java:109)
at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.handler$...$fabric-client-gametest-api-v1$postRunTasks
at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.runServer
```

Test thread, waiting at the phaser inside `close()`:
```
at net.fabricmc.fabric.impl.client.gametest.threading.ThreadingImpl.enterPhase(ThreadingImpl.java:109)
at net.fabricmc.fabric.impl.client.gametest.threading.ThreadingImpl.runTick(ThreadingImpl.java:288)
at net.fabricmc.fabric.impl.client.gametest.context.ClientGameTestContextImpl.waitFor(ClientGameTestContextImpl.java:195)
at net.fabricmc.fabric.impl.client.gametest.context.TestSingleplayerContextImpl.close(TestSingleplayerContextImpl.java:73)
```

So the render thread waits for the server to finish halting, while the server thread waits at the phaser for the render thread, which has left the phaser to run the disconnect. No mod frame is on any of the three stacks.

**Notes**
- The tests that hung close a world whose server may still be generating chunks (Terralith worldgen, C2ME storage threads).
- I have not yet seen it in a run without the other mods, because I cannot reproduce it at will. I can run with a reduced mod set if that helps.
- Full thread dumps are available on request.

issues.title: De-Hardcoding More Items
issues.body:
APIs for shears and other similar hardcoded items have been proposed before, but no action was made on them. It was recently brought up again on the the Docs, and checking in again, changes in 26.3 make some of the Shears implementation far more trivial, and the rest become trivial. The one decision worth making (beyond whether FAPI should do this, I suppose) is whether these should be adjusted to point to convention tags or the currently still existing classes e.g `BowItem`, `FishingRodItem`. I'm leaning towards the convention tags myself. 

Below are a list of places that would need mixins or data replaced:
- **Fishing Rods**: 
	- `FishingHook#shouldStopFishing` has two hardcoded checks for `Items.FISHING_ROD`. This ought to just be fixed, anything that extends `FishingRodItem` should be safe.
- **Bows**: 
   - `FirstPersonHandsAndItems#evaluateWhichHandsToRender` has two hardcoded checks for `Items.BOW`, handling whether the offhand is shown.
    - `AbstractClientPlayer#getFieldOfViewModifier` has one hardcoded check for `Items.BOW`,  handling zoom-in logic. This one feels important as well.
   - `RangedBowAttackGoal#isHoldingBow`, `AbstractSkeletonRenderer#extractRenderState`, `AbstractSkeletonRenderer#getArmPose`, `AbstractSkeleton#performRangedAttack` , `AbstractSkeleton#reassessWeaponGoal`, `AbstractSkeleton#canUseNonMeleeWeapon`  all have hardcoded checks for `Items.BOW`, important if Skeletons should shoot from these bows.
- **Shears**
   - `Bogged#mobInteract`, `PumpkinBlock#useItemOn`, `MushroomCow#mobInteract`, `Sheep#mobInteract`, `SulfurCube#mobInteract`,  `BeehiveBlock#useItemOn`, `CopperGolem#mobInteract`, `SnowGolem#mobInteract`,  `LeashFenceKnotEntity#interact` all have hardcoded checks for `Item.SHEARS` for determining whether the player can shear this entity
   - `TripWireBlock#playerWillDestroy` has a hardcoded check for `Item.SHEARS` for determining whether can safely mine/disarm the tripwire without setting it off
   - `LootPredicates` defines a `PLAYER_CAN_SHEAR` predicate used for loot tables. This one's new, but is reuseable data that can be safely modified/overriden with our shears tag, removing the need to modify every loot table!

issues.title: [Feature Request] Add transfer API support for container entities
issues.body:
Fabric API's `transfer-api` package is great for fine-tuning extraction and insertion of items/fluids into block and item containers. However, the same logic is currently not available for entity containers, e.g. modded variants of the vanilla Chest Boat. While the `Container` of such an entity can be wrapped by Fabric API's `ContainerStorage`, making it compatible with the transfer API, there is no way for other parts of the game, like hoppers or modded interfaces, to access this wrapper, since there is no entity equivalent to `BlockApiLookup<Storage<ItemVariant>, @Nullable Direction> SIDED` and `ItemApiLookup<Storage<ItemVariant>, ContainerItemContext> ITEM` within the transfer API.

Since an `EntityApiLookup` class already exists within the `lookup` api, this can likely be used to manage entity item/fluid transfers within the `transfer` api. Updating the mixins of the Hopper, Dropper and Crafter classes would also be required to ensure that vanilla blocks are able to interact with entities that expose their container solely through the transfer API.

issues.title: BiomeModificationContext.EffectsContext mutates BiomeSpecialEffects in place, so consumers that cache effects can't detect changes
issues.body:
EffectsContextImpl (e.g. setGrassColorOverride) assigns directly to fields on the biome's existing BiomeSpecialEffects instance after the Biome has been constructed. Code that caches values derived from the effects and invalidates by object identity never sees the change. Sodium does this: its BiomeMixin caches the grass and foliage colors in the Biome constructor and only refreshes when specialEffects is a different object, so overrides set through BiomeModifications don't render with Sodium installed.

Full description and repro: https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/3946

Environment: Minecraft 26.2, Fabric API 0.161.0+26.2, Sodium 0.9.2+mc26.2.

issues.title: Armor layer keeps the last player render state, which keeps the old world in memory (with EntityCulling)
issues.body:
**Versions**
- Minecraft 26.3, Fabric Loader 0.19.5
- Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3 (fabric-rendering-v1 27.0.14)
- EntityCulling 1.11.2 (includes TRansition 1.0.25)
- Java 25

**Issue**

After leaving a world, that world stays in memory (about 45 MB in my testing, render distance 16). It stays in memory even if you play a new world.

`HumanoidArmorLayerMixin` in fabric-rendering-v1 saves the last render state it drew in a field and never clears it.
TRansition (inside EntityCulling) makes every render state point to its entity. Together, the saved render state keeps
the old player, and the player keeps the whole old world.

Path found in a heap dump:

```
EntityRenderDispatcher.playerRenderers → player renderer layers
  → HumanoidArmorLayer.humanoidRenderState   (Fabric API)
  → EntityRenderState.transitionEntity       (TRansition)
  → LocalPlayer → ClientLevel
```

**Reproduce**

1. Install Fabric API and EntityCulling.
2. Join a singleplayer world, wear some armor, then open and close your inventory.
3. Save and Quit to Title, then join a world again and stay in first person.
4. Run `jcmd <pid> GC.class_histogram`. There are 2 `ClientLevel` and 2 `LocalPlayer`. Without EntityCulling there is 1 of each.

issues.title: Client GameTest can lock to 20FPS because the render thread blocks waiting on integrated server tick pacing
issues.body:
*AI Disclosure:* The reproduction mod is generated by AI. This is not an automated bug report. I encountered this naturally and wanted to report it.

By opening and closing 20 identical worlds, I can begin to observe that some worlds will lock to exactly 20 FPS while target FPS remains unlimited. Spark profiling shows that during the lock, the render thread spends a lot of its time blocked inside GameTest's phase synchronization logic while the server thread is in its normal server tick pacing wait.

The repro mod also has an experiment that bypasses the normal server tick pacing sleep. The server instead waits on GameTest's synchronization with client ticks, without blowing past 20 TPS. With it enabled, 0/20 worlds locked to 20 FPS.

Related to #5623 

Attached is the repro mod and reports I generated using it.

issues.title: Client game tests: closing a singleplayer world can deadlock (`IntegratedServer.halt` waits on the server thread while the server is parked in the tick phaser)
issues.body:
fabric-client-gametest-api-v1 6.0.2+0f4f1dca9e (Fabric API 0.161.0+26.2) and 0.161.0+26.3; Fabric Loader 0.19.5; JDK 25.
The threading code involved is unchanged on the default branch.

Rarely (about once in several hundred CI runs for us, more often when the game is paused), a client game test hangs forever
in `TestSingleplayerContext.close()`, or in any `Minecraft.disconnect(...)` run from `runOnClient` while in singleplayer.
Thread dump:

```
"Render thread": CompletableFuture.join <- BlockableEventLoop.executeBlocking <- IntegratedServer.halt
    <- Minecraft.disconnect <- MinecraftMixin lambda$deferDisconnect <- Minecraft.postRunTasks (postRunTasksHook)
"Server thread": Phaser.arriveAndAwaitAdvance <- ThreadingImpl.enterPhase <- MinecraftServerMixin.postRunTasks
    <- MinecraftServer.runServer
"Test thread": Phaser.arriveAndAwaitAdvance <- ThreadingImpl.enterPhase <- ThreadingImpl.runTick
    <- ClientGameTestContextImpl.waitFor <- TestSingleplayerContextImpl.close
```

Cause: `MinecraftMixin#deferDisconnect` moves the disconnect to the next `PHASE_TICK`. There
`Minecraft.disconnect(Screen, boolean, boolean)` calls `IntegratedServer.halt(false)` before the busy-wait loop that
`onDisconnectBusyWait` hooks, and `halt` blocks in `executeBlocking` until the server thread runs its task. In the same
tick phase the server thread runs `waitUntilNextTick`, which runs queued tasks only while `haveTime()`
(`MinecraftServer.shouldRun`); once its queue is empty and the tick is due it returns and parks in
`MinecraftServerMixin#postRunTasks` → `enterPhase(PHASE_TEST)`. If the client submits the halt task after that point (a
paused integrated server ticks in almost no time), the task is never run, and the client never reaches the phaser.

Deterministic reproduction: open a singleplayer world, register a `ClientTickEvents.START_CLIENT_TICK` callback that sleeps
1 s and then calls `Minecraft.getSingleplayerServer().halt(false)` (what `Minecraft.disconnect` does), then
`context.waitTicks(1)`: it hangs every time with the stacks above.

Possible fixes: keep the client in the phase logic while it waits for the server in `halt` (as `onDisconnectBusyWait` does
for the busy-wait after it), e.g. run the deferred disconnect's `executeBlocking` as a submit plus a loop of
`postRunTasks()` until the future is done; or have `MinecraftServerMixin#postRunTasks` keep running server tasks
(`managedBlock`) while a client `executeBlocking` is pending instead of parking. Workaround we use: before closing, queue a
server task that runs `server.managedBlock(() -> !server.isRunning())`, so the server keeps running tasks until the halt has
happened.

Our workaround in context: https://github.com/chaotix345/rigtune/blob/main/src/gametest/java/io/github/chaotix345/rigtune/gametest/GameTestWorlds.java

issues.title: Client events for received titles and subtitles in fabric-message-api-v1
issues.body:
`ClientReceiveMessageEvents` covers chat and game messages, but there is no client event for titles. `ClientPacketListener#setTitleText`, `setSubtitleText`, `setTitlesAnimation` and `handleTitlesClear` hand the packet straight to `Hud#setTitle`, `setSubtitle`, `setTimes` and `clearTitles`, and `Hud` keeps `title`, `subtitle` and `titleTime` private with no getter. A mod that wants to react to a title the server shows (log it, filter it, wait for it, read it aloud) currently has to mixin into `Hud` or reflect on those fields.

I could not find an existing issue or PR for this.

### Proposal

Add title events to `fabric-message-api-v1`, in the shape of the existing game-message events:

```java
// in ClientReceiveMessageEvents
Event<AllowTitle> ALLOW_TITLE;     // boolean allowReceiveTitle(Component title)
Event<Title> TITLE;                // void onReceiveTitle(Component title)
Event<AllowSubtitle> ALLOW_SUBTITLE;
Event<Subtitle> SUBTITLE;
Event<ClearTitles> CLEAR_TITLES;   // void onClearTitles(boolean resetTimes)
```

- Fired from a `ClientPacketListener` mixin at the head of the four packet handlers, so "receive" means the same thing as for `GAME`: the server sent it, before the HUD is touched.
- `ALLOW_*` returning `false` cancels the handler. There is no `MODIFY_*`: like the `ALLOW_GAME` docs suggest for overlay, a mod that wants a different title returns `false` and calls the public `Hud#setTitle` / `setSubtitle` itself.
- `CLEAR_TITLES` passes the packet's `shouldResetTimes()`.

`ClientboundSetTitlesAnimationPacket` (fade in / stay / fade out) could get an event too, but no use case needs it yet, so I would leave it out until one does.

Related: `ClientboundSetActionBarTextPacket` also bypasses the message events. `ALLOW_GAME`/`GAME` with `overlay = true` only see action bar text sent as a system chat message with the overlay flag, not the dedicated packet, which `ClientPacketListener#setActionBarText` passes directly to `Hud#setOverlayMessage`. That could be folded into this or fixed separately.

### Real-world case

A client mod that scripts a player for recordings needs to know when the server's plugin has shown a given title, and today reads `Hud`'s private fields for it: https://github.com/mc-chat-app/wishblock/blob/main/recorder/mod/src/main/kotlin/net/wishblock/recorder/Recorder.kt#L557-L570

Happy to open a PR with the events, mixin, and a testmod entry if this is in scope.

issues.title: Locator Bar waypoint rendering cannot be modified using HudLayerRegistry
issues.body: **Description of issue**: The rendering of the waypoints that mark players (or other custom entities) on the Locator Bar cannot be modified using the HudLayerRegistry contained within the `fabric-rendering` module of Fabric API. So for scenarios where you want to prevent rendering of the hotbar and everything closeby, you can hook into and modify rendering of the info bar background, but not its foreground, which at the time of writing only affects Locator Bar waypoints. Below is a screenshot of all usually visible hotbar-related GUI elements, and a screenshot where all available elements are hidden and the Locator Bar waypoint still shows up. **Code Analysis**: Within the many `WrapOperation` mixins of the `GuiMixin` class that handles vanilla hud elements, and especially the ones targeting method calls within the `extractHotbarAndDecorations` method, there is no mixin and associated vanilla hud element that wraps the call to `ContextualBarRenderer#extractRenderState`. This was likely an oversight from when the Locator Bar was first introduced in 1.21.6. **Suggested Fix**: The most backwards-compatible way to fix this would be adding a new `VanillaHudElements` field, e.g. `INFO_BAR_FOREGROUND`, through which the info bar foreground rendering can be controlled, without modifying the other fields. Alternatively, the info bar foreground rendering can also be made toggleable through the already existing `VanillaHudElements.INFO_BAR` field. If either solution is deemed appropriate, I can create a Pull Request to address this issue. Figure 1: Hotbar and locator bar visible during regular gameplay. Figure 2: Hotbar and related GUI elements toggled off through HudElementRegistry, with the locator bar waypoint still visible.

issues.title: Datagen never exits on success — JVM hangs after all providers complete (MC 26.2)
issues.body:
# Datagen never exits on success — JVM hangs after all providers complete (MC 26.2)

## Summary

`runDatagen` completes successfully, writes every file correctly, and then hangs
forever. The JVM never exits because non-daemon executor threads are still
parked. Only a kill ends the process.

`FabricDataGenHelper.run()` calls `System.exit` **only on failure**. On success
it returns normally and relies on the JVM exiting on its own — which cannot
happen while non-daemon pools are alive. Vanilla's `net.minecraft.data.Main`
guards against exactly this by ending with `Util.shutdownExecutors()`; the
Fabric datagen path has no equivalent.

The practical effect is that **a successful datagen run is indistinguishable
from a hung one**, and the exit code cannot be used as a success signal. That
makes datagen unusable in CI without a workaround.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Minecraft | 26.2 |
| Fabric Loader | 0.19.3 |
| Fabric API | 0.158.0+26.2 |
| `fabric-data-generation-api-v1` | 25.5.0+aed122aa9e |
| Java | 25 (Temurin) |
| Gradle | 9.5.1 |
| Loom | Architectury Loom 1.17.491 (multiloader project) |

## Reproduction

1. Configure datagen via `fabricApi.configureDataGeneration { }`.
2. Run `./gradlew runDatagen`.
3. Observe the run complete — all providers report, files are written:

```
[main/INFO] (Minecraft) All providers took: 150 ms
[main/INFO] (Minecraft) Caching: total files: 7, old count: 0, new count: 7, removed stale: 0, written: 7
```

4. The Gradle task never returns. The JVM stays alive indefinitely.

## Evidence

**`FabricDataGenHelper.run()` only exits on the failure path.** Disassembly:

```
public static void run();
   0: invokestatic  #7   // Method runInternal:()V
   3: goto          25
   6: astore_0                      <-- catch Throwable
   7: getstatic     #14  // LOGGER
  13: ldc           #24  // String "Failed to run data generation"
  16: invokeinterface #26 // Logger.error
  21: iconst_m1
  22: invokestatic  #32  // System.exit(-1)
  25: return                        <-- success path: plain return
  Exception table: 0 to 3 -> 6, Class java/lang/Throwable
```

**Vanilla's `net.minecraft.data.Main` shuts executors down explicitly:**

```
302: invokestatic #155 // Method net/minecraft/util/Util.shutdownExecutors:()V
```

`Util.shutdownExecutors()` calls `shutdownAndAwait` on both `BACKGROUND_EXECUTOR`
and `IO_POOL`.

**Thread dump of the hung JVM.** `main` has returned — `DestroyJavaVM` is
running — and 37 non-daemon threads remain parked:

```
"DestroyJavaVM" #79 ... java.lang.Thread.State: RUNNABLE

"pool-1-thread-1" #44 ... java.lang.Thread.State: WAITING (parking)
    at jdk.internal.misc.Unsafe.park(Native Method)
    at java.util.concurrent.LinkedBlockingQueue.take(LinkedBlockingQueue.java:435)
    at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.getTask(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1016)
    at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1076)
```

All 37 are idle `ThreadPoolExecutor` workers in `pool-1` and `pool-2`.

## Note on attribution

I have not isolated which component owns `pool-1`/`pool-2`. The generic
`pool-N-thread-M` naming and the `LinkedBlockingQueue` backing indicate
`Executors.newFixedThreadPool`, which does **not** match `net.minecraft.util.Util`
(that uses `newCachedThreadPool` and a `ForkJoinPool`). So these may not be
Minecraft's own pools, and this was observed in an Architectury multiloader
project rather than a plain Fabric template — worth confirming there.

That said, the asymmetry stands regardless of ownership: vanilla's datagen entry
point defends against surviving non-daemon executors and Fabric's does not, so
whatever creates them, the successful path currently has no way to terminate.

## Impact

Datagen cannot be used in CI as-is. A green run hangs until the job timeout,
and because success produces no exit code, the only robust signal is the
generated output itself. Our workaround polls the `.cache` directory for the
expected file count, then kills the JVM — a lot of machinery for what should be
`./gradlew runDatagen`.

## Suggested fix

Call `Util.shutdownExecutors()` (or the appropriate shutdown for whichever pools
survive) at the end of the success path in `FabricDataGenHelper.run()`, or
mirror the failure path with an explicit `System.exit(0)` once generation has
completed and all output is flushed.

issues.title: Block outline event mixin assumes old buffer instance stays relevant
issues.body:
This issue is relevant to Minecraft 1.16.5 - 1.20.6.

## Current behaviour

When rendering the block outline, we have the following steps:

1. Minecraft requests a buffer for `RenderType.lines()`
2. Fabric API fires block outline event, during which the buffer may become inactive when other render types are requested
3. Fabric API requests `RenderType.lines()` buffer
4. Minecraft renders the block outline to the original buffer instance

Importantly, Fabric API does not update the buffer reference, only requesting a buffer for `RenderType.lines()`.
https://github.com/FabricMC/fabric-api/blob/43c8677721b24b77688d8ad7e2fda2680842ba7f/fabric-rendering-v1/src/client/java/net/fabricmc/fabric/mixin/client/rendering/WorldRendererMixin.java#L115-L124

## Issue

The current behaviour relies on the assumption that the original buffer instance stays relevant and is reset.
If the assumption is broken and a new buffer is created rather than the original buffer instance being reset, this leads to a crash when vanilla submits the block outline to the original buffer.

The vanilla `BufferSource` implementation will always return the same buffer instance that is simply reset between requests.
Although the assumption is true for the vanilla implementation, as far as I can tell, vanilla never makes the assumption.

In Minecraft 1.21, the `BufferSource` implementation was updated and broke the assumption, now potentially leading to a crash. The Fabric API mixin was updated in #3940 by updating the buffer reference to the newly requested buffer.

ImmediatelyFast has their own `BufferSource` implementation that breaks the assumption by potentially returning a new buffer instance. This leads to a crash with my Item Collectors mod that requests a buffer for a custom render type during the block outline event (https://github.com/SuperMartijn642/ItemCollectors/issues/35).

In my opinion, the assumption is rather unintuitive and it is not strange for ImmediatelyFast to return a new buffer instance rather than holding on to and resetting an old instance when a render type is requested.
I think #3940 is a simple change that can also be applied to 1.20.6 and below that makes the behaviour not rely on the assumption.

The relevant code was introduced in #1319 for 1.16.5 and updated in #3940 for 1.21, hence the issue affects 1.16.5 - 1.20.6.

issues.title: Proposal: Server Query API for Fabric
issues.body:
Minecraft already provides the GameSpy4 server query, and Fabric Loader already provides the complete list of loaded mods.

Currently these two existing facilities are not connected.

I implemented a small working proof of concept for Minecraft 26.2 that reads the loaded mods from Fabric Loader and exposes them through Minecraft's existing GS4 query.

No new protocol is introduced.
No custom query server is required.
The existing Minecraft GS4 query remains unchanged.

The proof of concept is running successfully on a real Fabric 26.2 server and can be read by existing GS4 clients.

Working proof of concept:
https://github.com/airgalaxie/Fabric-Modlister

I propose exposing Minecraft's existing server query through a small Fabric API module/hook, allowing mods to contribute query information without implementing their own mixins.

The repository is intentionally minimal and demonstrates the currently missing connection between Minecraft's server query and Fabric Loader.

issues.title: Evolve Enchantment Modification API

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
The Enchantment API uses the vanilla `Enchantment.Builder`, but it does not allow you to modify `Enchantment.Definition` (which is set in the builder's constructor), making it impossible to do the following:
- Change the lists of supported items *directly* (see below)
- Change the list of slots in which the enchantment works
- Change the parameters like experience cost, anvil repair cost, and others

However, we cannot just extend the vanilla classes (using Interface Injection, as we already do in the Loot Table API) because `EnchantmentEvents.MODIFY` occurs during registry loading, when tags have not yet been bound (which complicates modifying the list of supported items).

> Change the lists of supported items *directly*

Important note: `EnchantmentEvents.ALLOW_ENCHANTING` allows an item to be enchanted, but the event works with `ItemStack` instead of expanding `EnchantmentDefinition::supportedItems` and `EnchantmentDefinition::primaryItems`, which complicates post-processing and potentially makes mod compatibility worse.

I propose the following:
- Modify enchantments after the registries have been loaded, as we already do with the Biome Modification API
  - This will allow for modification without any restrictions and expansion of vanilla classes using Interface Injection
- Provide a similar convenient alternative to `EnchantmentEvents.ALLOW_ENCHANTING` that expands `EnchantmentDefinition::supportedItems` and `EnchantmentDefinition::primaryItems`
  - `EnchantmentEvents.ALLOW_ENCHANTING` is objectively still useful, so we cannot remove it
  - This will ensure that the list is as complete as possible (except for cases where modders do mistakes ofc)
    - Improve the docs. We can also write a migration guide or smth
- Maybe provide `EnchantmentEvents.ALL_LOADED` similar to the `LootTableEvents.ALL_LOADED`

In addition to making the code very similar to the Loot Table API, the Biome Modification API, [and the future Advancement API](https://github.com/FabricMC/fabric-api/pull/5499), which will simplify the code and reduce technical debt, the API will become more robust and cover all use cases.

**I also think this might not break the existing API.**
___
> Change the list of slots in which the enchantment works
> Change the parameters like experience cost, anvil repair cost, and others

I'm working on a mod that modifies existing enchantments, and, currently, I'm forced to use `ServerLifecycleEvents.SERVER_STARTED` + `EnchantmentAccessor` with field mutations. In other words, the concept described above already works and tested.
___
I interested to work on this.

issues.title: Fabric Permissions API's usage of Identifier heavily limits available character set
issues.body:
Hi Fabric team! 

While implementing the new permissions API in WorldEdit, we've run into a few roadblocks. The largest of which is that using `Identifier` as a base prevents most characters from being used. It's not uncommon for dynamic permission nodes to be based on player-input, sometimes directly relating to filenames, player names, etc.

In WorldEdit we've worked around this by using a custom form of "URL encoding" and forcing case insensitivity (https://github.com/EngineHub/WorldEdit/pull/2990) to allow those to function, but it creates fairly significant complexity for users trying to setup permissions.

As prior community permission systems across both Fabric & the rest of the ecosystem (Bukkit-based, etc) have historically been simple string checks, this might be an issue more likely to affect older mods more frequently than newer ones. I also apologise for not bringing this forward during the initial implementation, I was not aware this permission API existed until ~5 days ago.

VeteranPack (2) — Modded signs overview part 2: continuation of the same row. Nature's Spirit x2, Deeper and Darker x2, Biomes O' Plenty x2, Regions Unexplored x2 and Vinery all render correctly. Note: Ghosts and Mystic Biomes are not in VeteranPack and therefore do not appear in these screenshots. (Because of the World Port from ModernPack to VeteranPack) VeteranPack (3) — Vanilla signs: all render correctly, identical to ModernPack. VeteranPack (4) — Break particles (green): particles from a correctly rendering sign show the expected texture. The full panel is visible in the background. VeteranPack (5) — Break particles (pink): same as above with a different wood type. All modded sign panels visible in the background. VeteranPack (6) — Break particles (dark brown with red sparks): same as above with a different wood type. VeteranPack (7) — Panoramic overview of the entire sign row. All panels visible. Particles visible in the foreground from a sign being broken. An additional anomaly was observed comparing the same sign across both packs (see VeteranPack (3) and ModernPack (7)). In VeteranPack, one modded sign renders with its correct panel visible but has a second panel of the same color overlapping it — larger and without texture applied — partially obscuring the text. The same sign in ModernPack renders perfectly with only the modded panel and fully legible text. This means there are actually three distinct failure modes visible across the two packs: correct rendering (ModernPack, a few signs), invisible panel with floating text only (ModernPack, most modded signs), and double panel rendering where a larger untextured version of the same panel overlaps the modded one (VeteranPack). This range of symptoms further supports a sign material or WoodType registration issue rather than a simple missing model. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Create a Fabric 1.20.1 instance with multiple biome mods that add custom wood types (Biomes O' Plenty, Oh The Biomes We've Gone, Nature's Spirit, Regions Unexplored, Better Nether, Better End, Farmer's Delight, etc.) 2. Enter a world in creative mode 3. Place standing signs from various modded wood types 4. Observe that many sign panels are invisible while only the text floats (Too many Mods to replicate the issue) ## Key observations - Particles are correct when breaking invisible signs: the wood texture appears in the break particles. This confirms the texture is loaded and the issue is in the panel model rendering, not in texture loading. - Signs from Supplementaries (both hanging signs and way signs) work correctly with the same modded wood types that produce invisible standing and wall signs. - The issue is consistent but selective: in ModernPack, Maple Delight, Vinery Sign and one Mystic Biomes sign always render correctly while all others from the same and different mods are always invisible. The set of affected signs does not change between sessions, after mod updates, or after removing individual mods. - Same world, different result: using the exact same saved world in VeteranPack produces correct rendering for all the same sign types. - Shaders are not the cause: tested with shaders completely disabled, issue persists. - Resource packs are not the cause: tested with all resource packs disabled, issue persists. - EBE is not the cause: tested with Enhanced Block Entities completely removed, issue persists. ## Comparison between working and broken modpack ModernPack (broken): 648 mods, Fabric Loader 0.19.3, signs.png-atlas 1024x1024x4 VeteranPack (working): 647 mods, Fabric Loader 0.19.3, signs.png-atlas 1024x1024x4 Shared mods: 491 with identical project ID and version ID, zero version differences between the two packs. The atlas sizes are identical between the two packs, ruling out atlas overflow as the cause. ## Mods excluded by testing (disabled or removed individually, issue persists in all cases) The following mods were each individually disabled or fully removed from the pack. In every case the bug persisted unchanged. Rendering and optimization mods: - Enhanced Block Entities (EBE) — removed entirely, including all config options (Enhanced Signs off, Experimental Signs off, Smart mode — all tested individually) - ImmediatelyFast — removed entirely - Shaders (Complementary Unbound + Euphoria Patches) — disabled entirely - All resource packs — disabled entirely Wood/block content generation mods: - Every Compat — removed entirely including the generated resource pack cache on disk - All More X Variants family mods — disabled as a group (More-Compatibility-Variants-OTBWG, more-compatibility-variants-bop, more-compatibility-variants-bx, more-compatibility-variants-ns, more-compatibility-variants-lets-do, MoreBeehiveVariants, MoreBedVariants, MoreBarrelVariants, MoreBookshelfVariants, MoreChiseledBookshelfVariants, MoreComposterVariants, MoreFurnaceVariants, MoreGrindstoneVariants, MoreJukeboxNoteblockVariants, MoreLecternVariants, MoreLoomVariants, MoreShieldVariants, MoreSmokerVariants) - ARRP (Advanced Runtime Resource Pack) - Fusion (Connected Textures) - SomeMoreBlocks - Adorn - arts_and_crafts - another_furniture - Cluttered - furnish Seasons mods: - Fabric Seasons and all compat mods (fabric-seasons-croptopia-compat, fabric-seasons-delight-compat, fabric-seasons-delight-refabricated-compat, fabric-seasons-extras, fabric-seasons-naturesspiritcompat, fabric-seasons-terralith-compat, seasonal_lets_do) ## Hypothesis The consistent but selective nature of the bug (always the same signs work, always the same ones do not, regardless of session or individual mod changes) strongly suggests a WoodType or sign material registration order issue. Modded wood types registered in a conflicting order may fail to obtain a valid sign material or texture mapping in the SignBlockEntityRenderer, while those registered earlier succeed. Hanging signs likely use a different registration code path that is not affected by this ordering issue. The fact that VeteranPack (647 mods) does not exhibit the issue while ModernPack (648 mods) does supports a threshold or ordering effect tied to the number of registered WoodTypes. ## Log excerpt (ModernPack) ``` [Render thread/INFO]: Created: 1024x1024x4 minecraft:textures/atlas/signs.png-atlas [Render thread/ERROR]: No data fixer registered for biomeswevegone:sign [Render thread/ERROR]: No data fixer registered for biomeswevegone:hanging_sign [Render thread/ERROR]: Parsing error loading recipe ns_fd_rc:cutting/framed_paper_sign com.google.gson.JsonSyntaxException: Unknown item 'natures_spirit:framed_paper_sign' ``` ## Why we are opening this issue We have been investigating this bug for a long time and have exhausted every reasonable approach we could think of as modpack authors without access to the internals of the rendering pipeline. We systematically disabled and removed mods one by one and in groups, always with the same result: the bug persists regardless of which individual mod is removed. The full list of excluded mods is documented above. We tested with shaders disabled, with all resource packs disabled, and with Enhanced Block Entities removed entirely — none of these changed the behavior. The most puzzling aspect is that the exact same saved world, with the exact same mods that are shared between both packs, produces correct rendering in VeteranPack and broken rendering in ModernPack. Furthermore, the set of broken signs is always identical — the same signs are always invisible and the same ones always visible, regardless of session restarts, individual mod removals, or pack updates. The 491 shared mods are byte-for-byte identical versions. The only difference is the additional mods present exclusively in ModernPack, none of which — when individually removed — fix the issue. This points to something systemic rather than a single guilty mod: likely a registration ordering issue or a limit in how many WoodTypes can be correctly mapped to sign materials before some start failing silently. Since this is beyond what we can diagnose without deeper knowledge of how Fabric API handles WoodType and sign material registration, we are opening this issue hoping the Fabric team can shed light on whether this is a known limitation, a bug, or something that can be addressed at the API level. Any guidance, even just pointing us in the right direction, would be greatly appreciated. ## Mod lists Full mod lists for both packs are attached as text files. ModernPack_modlist.txt (broken, 648 mods) VeteranPack_modlist.txt (working, 647 mods) [ModernPackModlist.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29941208/ModernPackModlist.txt) [VeteranpackModlist.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29941207/VeteranpackModlist.txt)

issues.title: ScreenMouseEvents hook swallows mouse release event
issues.body:
ScreenMouseEvents swallows mouse release event, and `mouseReleased` in widgets are not called. Callback in `beforeMouseRelease` is called, so it forces people who wants to listen for release event use Fabric API's hook when unnessasary. This is confirmable in `0.141.4+1.21.11`, which is latest version for Minecraft 1.21.11, and I believe it will be same for any version later than that, as the changelog since that version doesn't mention this issue.

Current workaround that I settled around is:
```java
ScreenMouseEvents.beforeMouseRelease(this)
        .register(((screen, context) -> 
                screen.children().forEach(
                       widget -> widget.mouseReleased(context))));
```

issues.title: Fabric 19.3 Java C2 JIT compiler bug causing game crash on Minecraft 26.2
issues.body:
I think i figured out what is causing this crash to happen.

I think i found a Java 25 JIT compiler bug that gets triggered by Fabric Loader’s threading + classloading model during world generation on 26.2. Java 25’s C2 JIT compiler is generating bad native code for certain hot paths in NoiseChunk, DensityFunctions, and related noise interpolation. Fabric’s worker threads + mixin environment make the bug surface reliably, while plain vanilla does not. This is not caused by any mods that alter chunk generation code like C2ME, Noisium, Sodium, Lithium etc. They just make it happen faster/more often. I got the same bug with fabric on the prism launcher and Curse Forge.

issues.title: [Feature Request] Track active mod list and versions in world saves
issues.body:
While organizing my enormous pile of old saves, I noticed that there is no way to identify which mods were active when a specific world was last played. This is a huge issue since I normally run close to 100 mods, and reconstructing the exact modpack for a given save is close to impossible once the original game installation is deleted. 

While `fabricRegistry.dat` stores mod effects, there is no human-readable list of what mods (and their versions) were last used to load that specific save.

I propose that Fabric API automatically saves a list of currently active Mod IDs and their versions into the world save directory every time the world is saved. This in theory should be lightweight and minimally-intrusive.

I've thought of two ways to do this:

**Option A: Embed into `level.dat`**
Inject an NBT tag (e.g., `FabricModList`) directly into the world's `level.dat`.

I understand the Fabric team prefers to keep `level.dat` as close to Vanilla as possible. Large modpacks (300+ mods) could also bloat the file size, so I understand if you think this option is not viable.

**Option B: A separate `fabricModList.dat` file**
Save the mod list as a separate NBT file inside the world's `data/` folder. This is, in theory, non-intrusive, since fabric mods already write files to the `data/` folder. If the world is loaded in Vanilla, the file is simply ignored.

I'm open to start coding a proof-of-concept of this implementation if you believe either one of these options is a good idea. As I said, having something like this would help me immensely in organizing my old saves in a much better way and being able to play them again in the future without going through the headache of trying to find which mods were used on it.

issues.title: `ButtonList` is unable to handle screens with renderable only widgets
issues.body:
Screens have three different lists for handling widgets: `renderables`, `children`, `narratables`.
There are also three different methods for adding to them: `addWidget`, `addRenderableOnly`, `addRenderableWidget`.

Fabric's `ButtonList` computes its size from `renderables`, but adds widgets to all three lists.
This fails when an existing widget in `renderables` is not present in any of the other lists.

More details can be found in my comment here: https://github.com/Roundaround/mc-inventory-management/issues/60#issuecomment-4600140238

My suggestion is to remove `ButtonList` as a whole. It's needlessly complicated, the more proper approach is to simply add transitive CT entries for the three vanilla methods which are `protected` right now, so people can call them from `ScreenEvents.AFTER_INIT`.

issues.title: Fabric permissions api fails operator level checks when LuckPerms is installed
issues.body:
Specifically in [this method](https://github.com/FabricMC/fabric-api/blob/26.1.2/fabric-permission-api-v1/src/main/java/net/fabricmc/fabric/api/permission/v1/PermissionContextOwner.java#L91), fabric api tries to get the permission level of the player or command source.
The implementations of it will assume the player has zero operator permissions if the permission set is not an instance of `LevelBasedPermissionSet`.

https://github.com/FabricMC/fabric-api/blob/b9cacd723116221d9b9e1ce03f411efb7fe59282/fabric-permission-api-v1/src/main/java/net/fabricmc/fabric/impl/permission/CommandPermissionContext.java#L61-L63

https://github.com/FabricMC/fabric-api/blob/b9cacd723116221d9b9e1ce03f411efb7fe59282/fabric-permission-api-v1/src/main/java/net/fabricmc/fabric/impl/permission/EntityPermissionContext.java#L81-L85

LuckPerms replaces this permission set and delegates it with [this](https://github.com/LuckPerms/LuckPerms/blob/master/fabric/src/main/java/me/lucko/luckperms/fabric/listeners/FabricPermissionsListener.java#L49), making the instanceof check always fail.

As a mod author there are ways around this such as using the boolean fallback method instead and handling the default operator checks yourself in a slightly different way, like for example:

```java
Perms.check(source, perm, Permissions.COMMANDS_GAMEMASTER)

public static boolean check(CommandSourceStack source, Identifier perm, Permission fallback) {
    return source.checkPermission(perm, source.permissions().hasPermission(fallback));
}
```

issues.title: Resource Packs Don't Change Mod Assets in 26.1.x
issues.body:
I maintain a resource pack that adds mod support to the pack that I use, and I've discovered that as of 26.1.x, it no longer works. I checked the contents of the affected mods' assets folders, and they have not changed. The textures are all in the same place in the old and new versions.

Steps to reproduce (for demonstration purposes, I made a pack that only has assets for the Immersive Overlays mod, it should be attached at the bottom of this message)

1. Set up a 1.21.11 instance with Fabric, Fabric API, and Immersive Overlays.
2. Install the attached resource pack (but don't enable it yet).
3. In any world, grab a compass, map, clock, or any other item that triggers an overlay. The borders of the overlays are gray with rounded corners.
4. Enable the resource pack. The overlays should now have wood borders with squared corners.
5. Update the instance to 26.1.x (any of them works for this) and update both mods to compatible versions.
6. Check the overlays again, and the wood borders are gone.

This applies to any resource pack that alters mod resources. It doesn't matter where in the list the pack is, it just doesn't do anything in 26.1.x.

Here's the resource pack I tested with:
[immersive_overlays_test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28168303/immersive_overlays_test.zip)

issues.title: `fabric:remove` keys are not always optional.
issues.body:
`fabric:remove` entries should never be considered required according to the package-info spec.

> Entries within the fabric:remove field are handled after all of the current file's values are added to the tag. **These entries should never be required, meaning they will never throw exceptions if not present in the associated registry.**

However, when making the PR, I forgot to test this, and only just found out that I could not remove Villager Rebalance Villager Trade values when the Villager Rebalance was not enabled if **optional** was not specified.

Test this yourself with this!
```json
{
  "replace": false,
  "values": [
  ],
  "fabric:remove": [
	"minecraft:librarian/2/emerald_and_book_desert_enchanted_book"
  ]
}
```

issues.title: [26.1.2] `ServerEntityEvents.ALLOW_LOAD` makes it very easy to cause a chunk loading deadlock from calling `ServerChunkCache::getChunk`
issues.body:
The new `ServerEntityEvents.ALLOW_LOAD` event is basically identical to NeoForge's `EntityJoinLevelEvent` which has also suffered from this issue in the past. NeoForge resolved this by implementing a workaround for the underlying vanilla issue.

More information can be found here regarding NeoForge's approach, including a reliable way to reproduce the deadlock for testing.
https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium/issues/667

The deadlock is hard to trace, as no error is logged and only the server hangs, while the client remains able to move around. Leaving the world is no longer possible, the game becomes stuck on the `Saving Level` screen, so players will loose all unsaved progress.

Personally I did use an event like this in the past for replacing mobs upon spawning (e.g. vanilla adult skeletons with modded baby skeleton variants in [Tiny Skeletons](https://modrinth.com/mod/tiny-skeletons)) which involves calling `ServerLevelAccessor::getCurrentDifficultyAt` (required for `Mob::finalizeSpawn`) which then further down the line calls the problematic `ServerChunkCache::getChunk`. I believe this is a rather common use case.

I'm not sure what's the best way to go about this. At the very least the event documentation should warn about this rather severe issue.
Maybe a similar fix to NeoForge can be implemented to handle the root cause. I've personally done so in my Tiny Skeletons mod, the implementation could be copied over to Fabric if desired. Although it's worth noting that there are a number of mods which break it, namely Lithium and C2ME.

issues.title: [26.1.2] `EntityHitResult` in `UseEntityCallback::interact` should no longer be marked as `@Nullable`
issues.body: Vanilla has merged `Entity::interact` and `Entity::interactAt`, therefore the `EntityHitResult` parameter should no longer be able to be `null`.

issues.title: Fabric Pack Overlays ignore Minecraft Version Formats

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body: Minecraft's Pack overlays have min/max formats as their conditions, and while fabrics overlay conditions work differently than Minecraft's, still having the ability to apply based on mc version AND AnyModsLoaded (for example) would be great

There is a mod nammed [Click Crystals](https://github.com/clickcrystals-development/ClickCrystals) which is a notoriuous hacked client that claims its not but it provides its users a huge advantage in PvP. It basically is a fully dedicated macro mod and the worst part they have don everything they can to hide any fingerprints from the server going as far as not using any lang files as many detection mods use that to detect client mods.

This mod has bugged me as a server owner for a year now and i have tried every thing i could, learned modding to try to make my own mods and i did succeed through the translation probing method but click crystals deliberately does not use that to reduce its fingerprint so as a last ditch effort i request the fabric team to impliment some sort of api so tha the server can know what mods the user is using enableing us to prevent hackers in our servers

issues.title: Fabric API 26.1 / 26.1.1 version labeling confusion causing crashes
issues.body:
**Issue summary:**

It seems that Fabric API versions for Minecraft 26.1 and 26.1.1 are mixed up on Modrinth and CurseForge. Players using 26.1 may accidentally download 26.1.1 builds, which can cause crashes like `RendererManager not registered`.

**Observed versions:**

| Fabric API Version | Minecraft Version | Notes |
|------------------|-----------------|-------|
| 0.144.4+26.1     | 26.1            | Works fine |
| 0.145.2+26.1.1   | 26.1.1          | Marked 26.1.1 |
| 0.145.3+26.1.1   | 26.1.1          | Marked 26.1.1, but HMCL users on 26.1 may use this and crash |

**Crash example (simplified):**


java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException: Attempted to retrieve active rendering plug-in before one was registered.
at knot//net.fabricmc.fabric.impl.client.renderer.RendererManager.getRenderer(RendererManager.java:29)
at knot//net.fabricmc.fabric.api.client.renderer.v1.Renderer.get(Renderer.java:70)
at knot//net.minecraft.client.renderer.feature.BlockFeatureRenderer.handler$zmm000$fabric-renderer-api-v1$beforeInitBlockRenderer(BlockFeatureRenderer.java:605)


**Environment:**

- Minecraft 26.1 / Fabric Loader 0.18.5
- Fabric API as listed above
- Iris, Sodium, Lithium, and other client mods

**Expected behavior:**

Clear version labels for 26.1 and 26.1.1 so users don’t accidentally download incompatible builds.

**Suggested action:**

- Fix Modrinth/CurseForge version labels to clearly separate 26.1 vs 26.1.1 builds
- Optionally add a note in release descriptions warning users about co

issues.title: KeyBindingHelper only takes an net.minecraft.class_304 instead of KeyMapping (26.1)

labels.name: support
labels.description: Issues closed due to being a support request.

issues.body:
Hello, I am currently trying to update one of my projects to 26.1.  
  
Part of that was of course to finally migrate away from yarn using migrateMappings, as well as to correct any fabric api method names such as renaming WorldRenderEvents to LevelRenderEvents, etc.  
  
Unfortunately there is one fabric api package that seems to be broken, that being KeyBindingHelper.  
  
`KeyBindingHelper.registerKeyBinding()` requires an `net.minecraft.class_304` instead of a `KeyMapping`.  
  
I assumed this was just some gradle weirdness relating to sources so I cleared caches and all that, but the issue persists, so I assume it is an oversight or something else I missed.  
  
Specifically, I removed `$HOME/.gradle`, `.gradle` in the project directory, as well as `build` and `.idea`.  
  
Thank you.  
  
(This is on version `0.144.3+26.1` of fabric api.)

issues.title: TealSignTest calls vanilla method instead of API implementation
issues.body:
*Issue opened as requested by ModMuss in mod-dev-kotlin channel on Discord

In the [TealSignTest](https://github.com/FabricMC/fabric-api/blob/26.1/fabric-object-builder-api-v1/src/testmod/java/net/fabricmc/fabric/test/object/builder/TealSignTest.java) file, WoodType.register(...) is called to register the custom WoodType instead of Fabric's own WoodTypeBuilder.register(...), this might confuse modders who use the test mods as examples as the register(...) method is actually private in the vanilla WoodType class and is not directly callable outside of the API environment. My recommendation would be to use the API method instead so that modders who reference this file will understand what they need to do in order to register a custom wood type.

issues.title: Add component-friendly alternatives to FabricItem methods (e.g. events)
issues.body:
Nowadays you usually don't need to to make your own class for items, many things can be done with components. However, `FabricItem` requires you to have a subclass as the way you use it is by overriding the methods it adds.

Additionally, if Mojang continues to make items "data-driven" and, e.g., makes `Item` class a `record`, `FabricItem` would have to be removed and its features implemented in other ways.

I imagine `allowComponentsUpdateAnimation` and `allowContinuingBlockBreaking` can be replaced with something like `ClientItemEvents#SWAP_ANIMATION` and `ClientItemEvents#RESET_BREAKING_PROGRESS`.

`EnchantmentEvents#ALLOW_ENCHANTING` already exists doing similar thing to `FabricItem#canBeEnchantedWith`, but the latter is still directly called from some mixins.

`getCraftingRemainder` and `getCreatorNamespace` can also be replaced with new events or with some sort of registry.

issues.title: [Feature Request] Loot Pool Entry Iteration and Modification for `modifyPools`
issues.body:
## Summary

Mods need to modify existing loot pool entries during `LootTableEvents.MODIFY`—for example, to filter enchantments from `EnchantRandomlyLootFunction` or adjust other entry-level functions. Currently this requires reflection because the necessary APIs to iterate and modify pool entries are not exposed.

## Use Case

Mods that rebalance loot need to edit vanilla pool entries (e.g. replace loot functions on existing entries) before adding their own pools, all within the same `MODIFY` callback. Without entry-level access, mods must use `MODIFY_DROPS` and workarounds that are more fragile.

## Current Limitations

- `LootPool.Builder` has a private `entries` field (`ImmutableList.Builder<LootPoolEntry>`) with no public accessor.
- There's no way to create a builder from an existing `LootPoolEntry` (e.g. `ItemEntry`) to clone it with modified functions.
- `EnchantRandomlyLootFunction` has no public way to create a copy with a filtered enchantment list.

## Requested APIs

### 1. Expose pool entries for iteration

Add to `FabricLootPoolBuilder` (or equivalent):

```java
/**
 * Returns the entries currently in this pool builder.
 * Useful for iterating and cloning entries with modifications.
 */
List<LootPoolEntryContainer> getEntries();
```

### 2. Replace pool entries

Add to `FabricLootPoolBuilder`:

```java
/**
 * Replaces all entries in this pool builder with the given entries.
 * Use with getEntries() to iterate, modify, and replace.
 */
LootPool.Builder setEntries(Collection<? extends LootPoolEntryContainer> entries);
```

Or alternatively, a higher-level modifier:

```java
/**
 * Applies a modifier to each entry; entries are replaced with the modifier's result.
 * Return null to remove an entry.
 */
LootPool.Builder modifyEntries(Function<LootPoolEntryContainer, LootPoolEntryContainer> modifier);
```

### 3. Create a builder from an existing entry

Add to `LeafEntry` or `ItemEntry` (or a shared utility):

```java
/**
 * Creates a builder pre-populated from an existing entry, for cloning with modifications.
 */
static LeafEntry.Builder<?, ?> copyOf(LeafEntry entry);
```

### 4. (Optional) Filter enchantments in EnchantRandomlyLootFunction

Add to `EnchantRandomlyLootFunction` or its builder:

```java
/**
 * Creates a copy of this function with the given enchantments excluded from the pool.
 * If options is empty (all enchantments), resolves from registry first.
 */
EnchantRandomlyLootFunction withExcludedEnchantments(RegistryEntryList<Enchantment> exclude, RegistryWrapper.WrapperLookup registries);
```

## Environment

- Minecraft: 1.21.10
- Fabric API: 0.138.3+1.21.10
- fabric-loot-api-v3

issues.title: Storage.insert unintentionally deletes items whose DataComponents specify MAX_STACK_SIZE different from the Item type's default stack size
issues.body:
I found this bug while messing around with an Oritech build designed for moving Oritech's Portable Tank via the Oritech Item Pipes. 

There's an [issue on the Oritech repo](https://github.com/Rearth/Oritech/pull/706) which has detailed steps for reproducing the problem in Oritech, but here's the gist:

Oritech Portable Tanks store Fluids (implemented via the Fabric Fluids API). When crafted and initially empty, Portable Tanks can be stacked up to the standard limit of 64. However, when a Portable Tank has fluid content, the tank uses DataComponents.MAX_STACK_SIZE to change the individual tank's stack limit to 1. (That is, tanks with fluid in them are not stackable). 

The bug in question arises when a Portable Tank is moved into an inventory via Fabric's `Storage.insert()`. In the case where a Portable Tank with a given fluid content is moved into an inventory which already contains a Portable tank with identical fluid content (for example, two Portable Tanks with the 256B limit of some fluid), the second tank is deleted / disappears. 

~(Presumably this would occur for any item whose DataComponents specify a different stack size from it's default, but I don't know of another example to test with).~ Update: I confirmed this is not specific to Portable Tanks or Fluid storage. An easy way to reproduce the bug is with an item that has had a max_stack_size set with the give command - e.g. `/give @s diamond[max_stack_size=1]`. 

I've got a PR coming which will explain the problematic call stack in more detail - will add a link here shortly.

issues.title: AttachmentSyncException disconnects client when target entity is not yet loaded
issues.body:
Fabric API Version: 0.138.4+1.21.10 (fabric-data-attachment-api-v1 1.8.33)
Minecraft Version: 1.21.10
Fabric Loader Version: 0.18.4

Logs:
[2026-02-08-6.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25177095/2026-02-08-6.log)

Description:
When a mod registers a synced attachment (e.g. prometheus:fire_type), Fabric API's attachment sync system can disconnect the client from the server with an AttachmentSyncException: Received attachment change for unknown target! if the target entity is not currently loaded on the client.
This happens because AttachmentChange.tryApply() (line ~165) throws AttachmentSyncException when targetInfo.getTarget(world) returns null, and AttachmentSyncClient catches this exception and explicitly calls disconnect().

An entity may not be loaded on the client for legitimate reasons:
Race condition between entity tracking and attachment sync packets
Entity is in a chunk that was just unloaded
Server sends attachment data slightly before the entity spawn packet arrives

Steps to Reproduce:
Install any mod that registers a synced entity attachment (e.g. Prometheus with fire_type)
Play on a server with multiple players/many entities
Observe periodic client disconnects with the error: Received attachment change for unknown target! Attachment identifier: prometheus:fire_type

Expected Behavior:
The client should log a warning and skip the attachment update for the missing target, similar to how vanilla Minecraft handles ClientboundSetEntityDataPacket for untracked entities.

Actual Behavior:
The client disconnects from the server.

Relevant Code:
In AttachmentChange.java:
```public void tryApply(World world) throws AttachmentSyncException {    AttachmentTarget target = targetInfo.getTarget(world);    Object value = decodeValue(world.getRegistryManager());    if (target == null) {        // ... builds error text ...        throw new AttachmentSyncException(errorMessageText);    }    target.setAttached((AttachmentType<Object>) type, value);}```

In AttachmentSyncClient.java:
```try {    attachmentChange.tryApply(context.client().world);} catch (AttachmentSyncException e) {    AttachmentEntrypoint.LOGGER.error("Error accepting attachment changes", e);    context.responseSender().disconnect(e.getText());  // <-- disconnects the client!    break;}```

Suggested Fix:
When target == null in tryApply, log a warning and return early instead of throwing. This mirrors vanilla behavior where packets for unknown entities are silently dropped.

Temp Patch:
I have created temp patch mod that so far seems to take care of the issue and has made things like Flashback mod failure and Server disconnections from happening: https://github.com/pandasonic-collective/AttachmentSyncFix

issues.body:
Looks like mojang made RegistryDataLoader more async and now the mixin in thenApplyAsycn trig the event way too late, after entries are filled. I checked the 1.21.11 branch - the DataLoader mixin used to inject into list.foreach right before the loop did its anything.

Docs in DynamSetupCallback look also wrong cause "triggered before" is not true and the example does nothing


As a temp fix for post-loaded you could sub start/end datapack reload events, then foreach registry

issues.title: [Suggestion] Stacking registry aliases

labels.name: module: registry sync
labels.description: Pull requests and issues related to registry sync

issues.body:
Currently, `FabricRegistry#addAlias` does not stack aliases. I think it would make sense if they did stack.

For example, say you have a registry aliased with `minecraft:a` to `minecraft:b`, and `minecraft:b` to `minecraft:c`. Currently, `minecraft:a` does not link to `minecraft:c` in that chain.

In my opinion, I think adding that stacking alias behavior would be more intuitive.

-# (Apologies if this is the wrong place to suggest or incorrectly formatted, I'm not sure I have anything further to say either.)

issues.title: Expanding `c:hidden_from_recipe_viewers` to other registries

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body: While working on [RRV](https://github.com/cassiancc/ReliableRecipeViewer/), I felt the need to expand `c:hidden_from_recipe_viewers` to the `Enchantment` and `Potion` registries, with the effect of hiding enchanted books and potions from the recipe viewer index. If there is interest, it would be good to add this to Fabric API/NeoForge directly so that mods like [Enchantment Disable Tag](https://modrinth.com/mod/enchantment-disable-tag) or [Enchantment Disabler](https://modrinth.com/mod/enchantment-disabler) can disable an enchantment in one place without needing direct integration with up to 4 recipe viewers.

issues.title: Expand on UseBlockCallback

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Currently `UseBlockCallback` is pretty limiting in that it doesn't allow the distinction between using an item on a block or using the block itself. 
This then does not allow you to e.g. only disable one of the actions and you need to block everything or nothing.

An implementation example (server sided only) can be found here: https://github.com/Flemmli97/Flan/blob/1.21/fabric/src/main/java/io/github/flemmli97/flan/fabric/mixin/ServerPlayerGameModeMixin.java#L26-L65

Rewriting the current `UseBlockCallback` would be a breaking change though

issues.title: Debug API

labels.name: new module
labels.description: Pull requests that introduce new modules

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
## Summary

Debug API is a hypothetical toolkit for registering and using debug subscriptions and other debug tools Mojang have created.


## Motivation

Presently, Mixin is required to add your own debug subscriptions to entities and other game objects. Mixin is great, really, but at a certain point it becomes annoying, especially when you want to make a quick and dirty debug renderer and subscription, and at that point, you might as well use print debugging.


## Explanation

A Debug API would implement methods to register debug subscriptions on the client and server, potentially on existing game objects as well. This would make implementing debug renderers easier as modders could properly use `DebugValueAccess` on which we could also add an injected interface for more customization. This API would also have its own module for ease of maintainability.


## Drawbacks

This would add a new module (oh no!), further reducing performance in Fabric API development, and annoying the tater out of maintainers.


## Rationale and Alternatives

 - You could theoretically shove some of the described features into unrelated modules, but that would be more annoying to maintain.
 - This makes it easier for modders to create debug features with no hassle.


## Prior Art

See #5035 testmod.


## Unresolved Questions

 - Should we keep `DebugRendererRegistry` in `fabric-rendering-v1`? It's probably fine to stay there, but moving it here could also have benefits.
 - Should adding debug subscriptions on existing game objects be event-based or registry-based?
 - Is this even in scope for Fabric API?

issues.title: Injected Interface `FabricRecipeExporter` isn't implemented via mixin.
issues.body:
#4703 introduced the `FabricRecipeExporter` interface to the data generation API, which is injected into the `RecipeExporter` interface. The contributing guidelines state, that [alongside every injected interface should come a mixin which implements it](https://github.com/FabricMC/fabric?tab=contributing-ov-file#api-design-patterns-to-consider).

> - Interface injection requires both a `fabric.mod.json` custom value to make it visible in Minecraft source code, and a mixin to actually implement the interface at runtime.

This isn't the case for `FabricRecipeExporter` though. I believe this wasn't done, because vanilla Minecraft only uses the `RecipeExporter` during its data generation and Fabric API also only constructs instances with the new interface, also only during data generation. So this never lead to any issues during gameplay.

In my case, I'm using the various `RecipeJsonBuilder`s during normal game execution though, which then broke when invoking `offerTo` because a Fabric API mixin assumed the existence of the added method. My fix for that is currently to just have this implementation mixin in my mod, as you can see [here](https://github.com/RubixDev/YARRP/blob/40e6c500733a0d738889009b0ca7762049a0e54f/versions/1.21.1-fabric/src/main/java/de/rubixdev/yarrp/mixin/fabric/RecipeOutputMixin.java). I believe this should just be included in Fabric API itself, though, unless I'm missing something.

The affected branches are `1.21.1`, `1.21.5`, `1.21.6`, `1.21.7`, `1.21.8`, `1.21.9`, `1.21.10`, and `1.21.11` as far as I can tell.

If the fix is really just to add such a mixin, I'd be happy to open a PR.

Code change detection API

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Add an API to detect changes in library codebases (primarily Minecraft). This API would go in a new test-only module for unit testing (which we surprisingly don't yet have).

## Description

At an abstract level, when a unit test written with this API is first run, it will scrape some data from the library jar, write it to a file, and pass the unit test. This file should be committed to the repo. Each subsequent time the test is run, the same data is scraped from the library jar, and compared against the data already written to that file. If the data is the same, the test will pass, if it is different (which may happen when the library is updated and changed in a way you are interested in) then the test will fail. If the file is deleted, the test will run anew, write the new data to the file, and then the test will be passed until the data changes again.

Here are some examples of useful change detection tests of this format:
- **Decompilations of classes, or individual methods, with Vineflower** (requiring Vineflower to be on the test classpath). The source code generated by Vineflower will be written to the file.
- **Usages of a class, method, or field**. The library (or maybe the whole library classpath) will be scanned for usages of a particular class, method, or field. The usages will be sorted in some deterministic order and written to the file.
- **Implementations of a class or interface**. The library (or maybe the whole library classpath) will be scanned for implementations of a particular class or interface. The implementations will be sorted in some deterministic order and written to the file.

The API could be made extensible. Every one of this type of test basically asks for a `Supplier<String>` which returns some `String` constructed based on the current environment. The API could handle all the writing to files.

## Motivation

Normally when you're using a library, most changes of code that you depend on are caught by `javac` as compile errors, which remain the most significant aid to porting. However, compile errors are of no help when *transforming* code. Here, the mixin audit test helps a lot to make sure the mixins at least don't crash, but even if the mixins don't crash, they are prone to logic errors after porting. Additionally, if we ever have to copy vanilla code (which we usually try to avoid, but it's sometimes unavoidable), we would like to be notified when the code we copied from is updated so that we can update our copy.

- [LiquidBlockRendererMixin](https://github.com/FabricMC/fabric/blob/1.21.11/fabric-rendering-fluids-v1/src/client/java/net/fabricmc/fabric/mixin/client/rendering/fluid/LiquidBlockRendererMixin.java) is targeting code that is quite hostile to mixins, so we have resorted to several rather brittle injections that interact with each other via `@Share`. Mojang could easily change this method without us noticing until a user reports a bug about the API not working properly. If we listened for changes in the `render` method we would know straight away when porting.
- The fluid API would like to replace many, but not all, uses of `FluidTags.WATER`, and in differing ways. We have until now avoided making this part of the API due to the maintenance burden. Having a unit test keep track of uses of `FluidTags.WATER` would make this API feasible for us.
- `FluidHandlerRegistry` hardcodes `isBlockTransparent` to a copy of the vanilla code, also in `LiquidBlockRenderer`. Again we could listen for this change.

And it's not just Fabric API itself that could benefit:
- Lithium could listen for changes in methods they target so that their optimizations, and particularly their `@Overwrite`s, don't over time end up causing changes compared to vanilla behavior.
- The clientarguments library, which needs to copy most/all vanilla argument types for client-side use, could listen for changes in all those argument types, and for new argument type implementations.
- ViaFabricPlus, and also the ViaVersion team, can write tests to listen for changes affecting the protocol, player movement, and other things they need to be updated on.
- Clientcommands, which already has regression tests for this purpose, can be changed to use this API
- The bingo-extras mod I wrote uses mass ASM to replace all dimension checks so that vanilla dimension-specific features still work on fantasy mirror dimensions. It's somewhat risky to use mass ASM for this purpose and I am probably still missing some stuff because of it (for example the clock and the compass). Fantasy itself could possibly also benefit, not sure. I'm also likely not the only one who has written mass ASM or a ton of mixins for this exact purpose.
- Most likely many modders have over time winced at the duplication of code from vanilla or some brittle target and worried about what might happen when it changes. This API would bring them the option of doing it with a peace of mind when there is no other option.

## Prior art

### Vineflower

Vineflower itself has a suite of regression tests almost exactly like this, for a slightly different purpose: testing Vineflower. Their job is to make sure that changes to Vineflower don't have unexpected negative consequences to decompilation, and that any changes to the decompiler output in those tests are at least seen and acknowledged by the developer.

### clientcommands

Clientcommands has a suite of so-called regression tests, inspired by Vineflower and working in a similar way. They are more or less what I am proposing for this API, although the exact API could be refined a bit. The regression test can be found [here](https://github.com/Earthcomputer/clientcommands/blob/fabric/src/test/java/net/earthcomputer/clientcommands/test/EntityRandomCallHierarchyTest.java), with the output files [here](https://github.com/Earthcomputer/clientcommands/tree/fabric/regressionTests). My usecase is a little more complicated than most mods require, with `CallHierarchyWalker` walking up the usage tree multiple steps - most mods will only require the simple usage of one field/method. The regression tests have already caught multiple changes that I wouldn't have spotted otherwise without checking the call hierarchies manually for each port.

### MusicalCode

[MusicalCode](https://github.com/Earthcomputer/MusicalCode) is an older experimental project of mine for the purpose of listening for changes in vanilla code. This project was soon abandoned, and I consider clientcommands' regression tests experiment to be an overall better and more powerful method of listening for changes. Lithium briefly adopted MusicalCode in an attempt to solve their worries about their `@Overwrite`s getting out of sync.

### ViaVersion

ViaVersion and other protocol translators and protocol translator adjacent projects need to listen for changes beyond what would be caught by a simple compile error and mixin audit based port. An early tool to check for protocol changes, block and item changes, etc was [Burger](https://pokechu22.github.io/Burger/) by Pokechu22. Since then, KennyTV has developed a tool which dumps all `StreamCodec`s to a file, which can then be diffed.

issues.title: Resource Reloader v1 - SharedState Misses Some Tags on World Load

labels.name: module: resource loader
labels.description: PRs and issues related to the resource loader API

issues.body: Mojmap warning In 1.21.10 (FAPI 0.138.0+1.21.10), when using v1's SimpleResourceReloader, we are given the `SharedState` in the `prepare` method, which we can obtain lookups from. On regular resource reload, this is fine, but upon the first world load (see `WorldLoader#load`), our lookup is missing a lot of tags (using the item registry as an example). ```java HolderLookup.Provider delegate = store.get(ResourceLoader.RELOADER_REGISTRY_LOOKUP_KEY); ``` This is because on first world load, all tags are actually stored in `ReloadableServerResources`'s `postponedTags`, which I believe are only correctly put into future lookups after `updateStaticRegistryTags` is called. To combat this, I've come up with a temporary solution in https://github.com/ekulxam/Spectre/compare/12b765b..9636dbc#diff-13a335527dba6451d26a52a1e4bf66f9f68ad85da68cdb2cf30d0261f297e0cbR80, where I've stored the `List>` in the `SharedState` and then used it with the original lookup to create a special `HolderLookup.Provider` implementation. This implementation does correctly contain all tags (474 vs 16), but has the slight problem where the tags are actually not bound and the `HolderSet`s have no contents. This does work to some extent though, as loading in `#c:crops` in a dynamic creative tab gives I'm mainly asking for a less cursed solution that actually has populated tags upon resource reload. Perhaps we could delay resource reloading to after `updateStaticRegistryTags` and see if the lookup is given with the correct tags. This is arguably a minecraft bug, but I think Resource Reloader v1 has a good shot at fixing this.

issues.title: Invalid Interface Injection pretends to work in fabric dev environment

labels.name: wontfix
labels.description: This will not be worked on

issues.body:
Tested with MC 1.20.1, fabric 1.16.9, loop 1.9-SNAPSHOT, on intellij.

How to reproduce:

- Go through all the steps to inject an interface EXCEPT making the mixin. Say, into Enchantment.class
- Give the interface a default method and nothing else (probably not a required step)
- DO NOT create a mixin for the interface. The only usage of the interface so far should be in the fabric.mod.json
- somewhere else in the mod, check to see if the interface has been injected properly. In this example, you could hook into a player attacking with an enchanted item, and have something that logs a message if the enchantment extends your injected interface.

Expected behavior: Both in the fabric dev environment and when you build the mod and run it, say, in modrinth, the interface should fail to inject and the logging should say that no Enchantment extends your interface.

Actual behavior: In the development environment, the interface is successfully injected, even with no mixin. However, in the real environment it does not inject.

Main problem: Modders who do interface injection without the proper mixin will think that their mod works when it in fact does not.

Use case where it came up for me:
- I made Enchantment.class extends MyEnchantmentInterface. It had a default method that I wanted to override for a specific enchantment.
- When I created "MyEnchantment extends Enchantment" the class, I wrote a method override to extend the interface.
- I needed to also create the empty mixin @Mixin(Enchantment.class) public interface MyMixin extends MyEnchantmentInterface {}
- But I forgot, and encountered reports of a bug I could not reproduce until I added more logging, read the discord logs, and realized the mixin was required.

issues.title: Make the AttachmentType Object.equals check optional
issues.body:
https://github.com/FabricMC/fabric/blob/c920b084e3cc513b0b2754a15313ebb31a267872/fabric-data-attachment-api-v1/src/main/java/net/fabricmc/fabric/mixin/attachment/AttachmentTargetsMixin.java#L92

Apparently it's encouraged to make your AttachmentTypes immutable but that seems a bit dumb for large objects with lots of fields inside fields etc. If i want to change just one value, why recreate the entire object?

I suggest making the object.equals check optional. Just add a boolean to attachmentType, requiresImmutability, or whatever

I found a few workarounds around this issue, which all seem really bad

1) whenever i want to sync things, first set my object to an empty instance, before setting it to my real data, this avoids the stupid object equals check, this is bad because it syncs the data twice now
2) use the codec to load my object back and set that instead, this is a lot of overhead for a simple field change but it avoids the double sync
3) sync the data myself when i need to. 
4) wrap all my attachments into another object/record and increment a simple transient counter field, this should avoid the equals check 

Or is there a good reason to force immutability on attachments?
